_meta.indication: INTELENCE, in combination with other antiretroviral agents, is indicated for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in antiretroviral treatment-experienced adult patients who have evidence of viral replication and HIV-1 strains resistant to an NNRTI and other antiretroviral agents.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial comparing etravirine 200 mg BID plus an optimized background regimen (including darunavir/ritonavir) to placebo plus background regimen; Study C206 conducted primarily in the United States and Latin America.
pivotal_trials.population: Treatment-experienced HIV-1-infected patients with plasma HIV-1 RNA > 5000 copies/mL on a stable antiretroviral regimen for at least 8 weeks, with at least one documented NNRTI resistance-associated mutation and at least 3 documented primary PI mutations.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects with undetectable plasma viral load (< 50 HIV-1 RNA copies/mL) at Week 24
pivotal_trials.result: Trial TMC125-C206, Viral Load < 50 copies/mL (TLOVR) at Week 24: 170/304 (55.9%) TMC125 vs 119/308 (38.6%) placebo.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial identical in design to C206; conducted primarily in the United States and Europe.
pivotal_trials.population: Treatment-experienced HIV-1-infected patients with plasma HIV-1 RNA > 5000 copies/mL on a stable antiretroviral regimen for at least 8 weeks, with at least one documented NNRTI resistance-associated mutation and at least 3 documented primary PI mutations.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects with undetectable plasma viral load (< 50 HIV-1 RNA copies/mL) at Week 24
pivotal_trials.result: Trial TMC125-C216, Viral Load < 50 copies/mL (TLOVR) at Week 24: 183/295 (62.0%) TMC125 vs 129/296 (43.6%) placebo.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions were rash (any type) 16.9% vs 9.3% placebo and nausea 13.9% vs 11.1% placebo. The most frequent ADR of at least Grade 2 severity was rash (9.0%). Severe/life-threatening skin reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome, hypersensitivity reaction, erythema multiforme) were reported in <0.1% of subjects. A total of 2% discontinued due to rash.
target_moa: Etravirine is a non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI) of HIV-1 that binds directly to reverse transcriptase and blocks the RNA-dependent and DNA-dependent DNA polymerase activities by disrupting the enzyme's catalytic site.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; NDA 22-187 was not referred to an advisory committee because there were several previously approved agents in the NNRTI class and the safety/efficacy data did not pose particular concerns.

summary.text: Etravirine (Intelence), a second-generation NNRTI, received priority review as it meets an unmet medical need and was approved under accelerated approval regulations (21 CFR 314.510) based on Week 24 virologic response data from the DUET trials, with a requirement to submit Week 48 analyses to verify clinical benefit for traditional approval. The application was not referred to an advisory committee.

citations.quote: This NDA was submitted in July, 2007 and received a priority review because it meets an unmet medical need.

It is approved under the provisions of accelerated approval regulations (21 CFR 314.510), effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon labeling text (package insert, patient package insert and immediate container label).

This indication is based on Week 24 analyses from 2 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of INTELENCE™. Both studies were conducted in clinically advanced, 3-class antiretroviral (NNRTI, N[t]RTI, PI) treatment-experienced adults.
Submit study reports for Week 48 data analyses for the ongoing Phase 3 studies TMC125-C206 and TMC125-C216 to support the traditional approval of etravirine.

NDA 22-187 was not referred to an advisory committee for review because there are several previously approved agents in the non-nucleoside class of drugs, evaluation of the safety data did not reveal particular safety issues that were unexpected for this class, and the design and results of the safety and efficacy trials did not pose particular concerns.
